newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria short-term deposit rates rise.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria short-term deposit rates rise.

text.p: Demand for lev funds was high on Monday and the short-term interbank deposit rate rose despite a cut in the main interest rate, dealers said.
"Short-term depo rates tend to be higher than the long-term rates which is a practice in the developed markets," said a bank dealer.
The central bank cut its main interest rate to 10.12 percent simple annual or an effective annual 10.60 percent, in force from Monday.
The main interest rate was set at an effective annual 16.30 percent last week.

Overnight interbank depo rates rose to 12-14 percent annually from 11-12 percent on Friday while deposits for up to seven days were borrowed at a simple annual interest of 10-12 percent, down from 15-16 percent.
The average annual interbank deposit rate was 12.12 percent on Friday against 13.71 percent on Thursday, a central bank official said. -- Dessislava Popova, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
